subject: Basic Science
sourceFile: Copy of Basic Science & Tech BECE Syllabus - syllabusNG.txt
examFormat: The BECE Basic Science and Technology syllabus aims to help candidates gain a fundamental understanding of science and technology, apply scientific and technological knowledge to address modern societal needs, and be equipped with essential knowledge for further studies in science and technology. Basic Science and Technology is examined in four compulsory papers (I–IV). The Basic Science component is examined in Paper I, which has 60 multiple-choice questions covering Basic Science together with Physical and Health Education, with an allocated time of sixty minutes.
excluded: Syllabus.ng marketing ("About us", "About BECE"), eligibility, registration, grading table, table of contents and the FAQ chapter were left out. The Basic Technology, Physical and Health Education and Computer Studies themes of the same file are in their own subject files.
recommendedTexts: Progress in Basic Science — Rowland S. Chukwura et al. (Rasmed Publications, Ibadan)
Progress in Basic Science — Segun Adeniyi et al. (Rasmed Publications, Ibadan)
Current Basic Science for JS1–3 — N. N. Nwankwo et al. (MIS.FAV, Onitsha)

subtopics.name: Sanitation
objectives: Explain sanitation as an aspect of family health.

subtopics.name: Nutrition

objectives: Explain drug and substance abuse as a family health issue.

subtopics.name: Definition of air, soil and water pollution
objectives: Define air, soil and water pollution.

subtopics.name: Causes of air, soil and water pollution
objectives: Identify causes of air, soil and water pollution, e.g. domestic/industrial waste, fertilizers/insecticides, agricultural chemicals, non-biodegradable materials and oil spillage.

subtopics.name: Consequences of pollution
objectives: Describe consequences of pollution such as respiratory tract infection, water-borne diseases, destruction of soil organisms and poor plant growth.

subtopics.name: Control measures for pollution
objectives: State control measures for air, soil and water pollution.

objectives: Explain the meaning of matter and identify and classify matter.

subtopics.name: States of matter
objectives: Describe the states of matter.

objectives: State the characteristics of living and non-living things.

objectives: Give examples, characteristics and importance of plants and animals.

objectives: State the differences between plants and animals.

objectives: Classify non-living things into metals and non-metals.

objectives: Describe habitats and give examples.

subtopics.name: Adaptation of living things to their habitat
objectives: Explain the adaptation of living things to their habitat.

subtopics.name: Relationship between organisms in the same habitat
objectives: Describe the relationship between organisms in the same habitat.

subtopics.name: Uniqueness of human beings
objectives: Explain the uniqueness of human beings: reasoning, problem solving, observation, inquisitiveness, measurement and inference.

subtopics.name: Measurement of growth and development
objectives: Measure growth changes in height, weight and size.
Describe developmental changes: infancy, adolescence and adulthood.
State the characteristic features of stages of development.
Classify growth and development changes as temporary or permanent.

subtopics.name: Meaning of chemicals
objectives: Explain the meaning of chemicals.

subtopics.name: Classes of chemicals
objectives: Classify chemicals based on use (e.g. pharmaceutical/cosmetic, nuclear, industrial, laboratory) and on hazardous nature (highly hazardous and toxic, moderately hazardous and toxic, non-hazardous and non-toxic).

subtopics.name: Safety measures when using chemicals
objectives: Adhere to the manufacturer's safety instructions.
Follow safety guidelines for chemical storage and handling.
Observe and adhere to safety instructions on chemical packages.
Ensure proper labelling and storage of chemicals.

subtopics.name: Examples of family traits
objectives: Identify family traits such as skin colour, height and albinism.

subtopics.name: Dominant and recessive traits
objectives: Explain the meaning of dominant and recessive traits.

subtopics.name: Importance of family traits
objectives: State the importance of family traits in relation to intelligence, diseases, resemblance and family genealogy.

subtopics.name: Soil erosion
objectives: Define soil erosion.
State the causes of soil erosion.
Describe the control of soil erosion.

subtopics.name: Flooding
objectives: Describe drainage patterns.
State the causes of flooding.
Describe the prevention of flooding.
Explain the effects of flooding on the community and farmland.

subtopics.name: Bush burning
objectives: Identify practices influencing bush burning.
Describe the effects of bush burning, including economic consequences.
State regulations against bush burning.

subtopics.name: Deforestation
objectives: Give reasons for deforestation, e.g. commercial use and domestic firewood.
Describe the effects of deforestation on the environment.
State regulations on deforestation.

subtopics.name: Desertification
objectives: Define desertification.
Identify the geographical area affected by desertification.
State the causes of desertification, e.g. overgrazing, bush burning and cutting trees for firewood.
Describe control measures against desertification.

subtopics.name: Depletion of the ozone layer and its effects
objectives: Describe the ozone layer and its location in the atmosphere.
State the importance of the ozone layer.
Explain the effects of ozone depletion, e.g. global warming, greenhouse effect, ice melting and flooding.

subtopics.name: Control measures against ozone depletion
objectives: Explain regulation on the use of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs).
Explain the need to reduce bush burning.
Explain the control of burning in household activities.

subtopics.name: Effects of drug abuse
objectives: Describe effects of drug abuse, e.g. stomach upset, skin rashes, damaged nostrils and lungs, and injection abscess.

subtopics.name: Prevention of drug abuse
objectives: Explain ways of preventing drug abuse, e.g. inculcating coping skills, a healthy lifestyle and positive social interactions.

subtopics.name: Activities of drug control agencies (NAFDAC, NDLEA)
objectives: Describe the activities of drug control agencies such as NAFDAC and NDLEA.

subtopics.name: Misuse of herbal medicine
objectives: Explain the misuse of herbal medicine.

subtopics.name: Plant resources
objectives: Give examples of plant sources of resources, e.g. cash and food crops, dyes and drugs.

subtopics.name: Animal resources
objectives: Give examples of animal sources of resources, e.g. hides and skin and dairy products.

subtopics.name: Economic importance of resources from living things
objectives: State the economic importance of resources from living things to self and society.

topics.name: Resources from Non-Living Things
objectives: Give examples of solid minerals such as coal, limestone, gold and tin.
Identify the location of solid minerals in Nigeria.
State the economic importance of resources from non-living things.
topics.content: Sub-theme: Learning about your environment. Solid minerals such as coal, limestone, gold and tin; their location in Nigeria and economic importance.
